observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon D750 retail box with a USPS Ground Advantage shipping label attached.
Photo 0 also shows a Nikkor 50mm lens box and a Zhiyun gimbal box in the background.
Photo 1 shows the D750 box open, containing two user manuals (English and French) for the Nikon D750.
Photo 2 shows the interior of the box with two large objects wrapped in bubble wrap.
The camera body itself is not visible in any of the photos.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a USPS (United States Postal Service) shipping label on the box.
The box and manuals match, but the body is wrapped in bubble wrap in photo 2 and not seen.
The camera body is not visible; it is covered by bubble wrap in photo 2.

risks.risk: The item inside the bubble wrap may not be a Nikon D750 or may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo of the camera body out of the bubble wrap showing the model name.
risks.if_unproven: as an empty box or parts

risks.risk: The camera body may have significant physical damage or wear.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the front, back, top, and bottom of the unwrapped camera body.

risks.risk: The sensor may be scratched or dirty.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the sensor with the body cap removed.

risks.risk: The shutter may be near the end of its life (high shutter count).
risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count from a recent image's EXIF data.

proof_requests: Photos of the camera body out of the bubble wrap from all angles.
A photo of the camera turned on with the rear LCD screen active.
A photo of the camera sensor with the body cap removed.
response.reason: The seller has only provided photos of the packaging and manuals. The actual camera body is hidden inside bubble wrap, making it impossible to verify its identity, condition, or presence.
